$comment: GENERATED FILE — DO NOT EDIT. source: contracts/design/form.schema.yaml plus the closed lists resolved from contracts/metrics/ and contracts/policies/; generator: holdout.contracts.compilers.design_form; regenerate: make contracts.

decision_rule.description: What we will do with each outcome, declared before the period opens and applied unchanged when it closes. A rule that permits acting before max_duration has elapsed is refused with STOPPING_RULE_PERMITS_PEEKING. `if_refused` is mandatory because a refusal is an outcome, and a design with no plan for it invites the plan being made after the refusal arrives.

exclusions.description: Store ids with reasons, declared before assignment. Every exclusion is a degree of freedom, so each one carries a reason that can be read back.

filled_by.description: Attribution, not a design field. The engine reads it, records it and ignores it when deciding. All three sources are first-class.

hypothesis.description: One precise sentence — what changes, on what, measured by what. Imprecision here is not caught by any later check, because every later check takes the hypothesis as given.

intervention.description: What the two arms actually are. Control is never "nothing": the holdout runs the existing policy, because comparing against abandonment would inflate every uplift.

control.$comment: closed list `policy_refs`, resolved from the contracts at compile time. Do not edit: add or remove the contract instead.

treatment.$comment: closed list `policy_refs`, resolved from the contracts at compile time. Do not edit: add or remove the contract instead.

max_duration.description: A business constraint, not a statistical one. If the required sample does not fit inside it the design is refused with UNDERPOWERED_FOR_DURATION rather than quietly shortened.

mde.description: The smallest difference worth detecting, declared in advance. Declared afterwards it is whatever the data happened to show.

direction.description: A one-sided expectation must be declared before the period opens or not at all.

primary_metric.$comment: closed list `metric_ids`, resolved from the contracts at compile time. Do not edit: add or remove the contract instead.
primary_metric.description: From the metric contract — a closed list, never free text. An id outside the contract is refused at design with METRIC_NOT_IN_CONTRACT. The version is not chosen here: the version in force on the design date applies, and it applies permanently to this experiment even after the metric is superseded.

scope.description: Which categories, products and stores the experiment may touch.

products.description: Null means every product in the named categories.

stores.description: `all` means the whole corpus minus the exclusions. A list narrows it. Narrowing after the fact is what EXCLUSIONS_DEFINED_POST_HOC refuses.

unit.description: The unit of randomisation. It has no single correct answer, which is why a model may propose it — and whether the resulting design has the power it claims has exactly one, which is why code decides that.
